prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1314; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver was named on the policy as a person who may NOT drive the car.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured vehicle was reported in a collision at an intersection while turning left. The claimant has retained counsel, so all further contact is to go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police attended and confirmed a passenger was in the vehicle at the time. Independent witnesses and scene photographs match the described sequence of events, and the other driver has given the same account.

Entry 3: The claimant reports shoulder pain and has been seen by a physician. The injury is consistent with a collision of this type, and no earlier injury to that shoulder is known.

Entry 4: The vehicle inspection shows damage on a different side of the car and at a different height from the impact the claimant described, so the damage does not line up with the account given. Photos are on file for review.

Entry 5: The claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation so far, including the recorded statement and the call with counsel present.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a standard course and sessions tapered off as the claimant improved. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: The records check shows the driver at the time of loss is named on the policy as not permitted to operate the vehicle. Referred to underwriting to review the named-driver position.

Entry 8: File reviewed. Liability remains open pending the resolution of the inspection discrepancy and the named-driver question. Next steps are to request the treating records and the attorney's demand package.
